item.title: Carmela Chillery-Watson became the youngest MBE recipient after raising funds for muscular dystrophy
item.description: Carmela Chillery-Watson became the youngest MBE recipient at eleven years old. She received the honour for her extensive fundraising and awareness work. This recognition celebrated her dedication to Muscular Dystrophy UK and the disabled community. Carmela's journey began after her diagnosis with a rare muscle-wasting condition at age four. Her continued advocacy aims to promote accessibility and support for those affected.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2022, Buffalo completed the first emerald shiner passage on the Niagara River; four years later...
item.description: The city of Buffalo is enhancing a fish passageway to facilitate the journey of emerald shiners to Lake Erie. By installing steel baffles along the seawall, this initiative aims to mitigate strong currents. This effort is part of a significant multi-million-dollar restoration project for the Niagara River Area, alongside transforming nearby industrial slips into crucial shallow-water habitats, all geared towards rectifying historic environmental harm in western New York.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Washington launches project to restore 270 acres of Skagit estuary habitat
item.description: In a significant environmental effort, the restoration of 270 acres of estuary habitat in the South Fork Skagit River is underway, starting from June 2026 and set to finish by fall 2028. This initiative focuses on enhancing the habitat for the endangered Puget Sound Chinook salmon, ensuring a sustainable ecosystem by reconnecting islands to tidal flows, and supporting various wildlife, including waterfowl and shorebirds.

item.title: 70 million years ago, Earth had 372 days a year, with days lasting 23 hours
item.description: Research into ancient shells has unveiled that Earth experienced a 372-day year around seventy million years ago. During the Cretaceous period, each day was approximately twenty-three hours and thirty-one minutes long. This study also examined the ancient Earth-Moon distance and revealed warmer ocean temperatures, with evidence of photosymbiosis. The mollusc fossil indicates it thrived for over nine years on a tropical seabed.

item.title: Amondawa tribe does not use weeks, months or years to describe time
item.description: The Amondawa tribe structures their daily living around significant events and life phases rather than fixed numbers of weeks or years. Their language features an absence of abstract units of time, showcasing a unique relationship between age and identity rooted in transitional life stages. This inquiry prompts a reevaluation of conventional beliefs regarding human perceptions of time.

item.title: Why are streamers calling out Twitch after ExtraEmily is named Ambassador despite backlash?
item.description: Twitch has sparked controversy by appointing ExtraEmily as a new Ambassador despite her history of unsafe driving during streams, leading to multiple suspensions. A particularly alarming incident involved her nearly colliding with another vehicle while live. This choice has prompted critics to question Twitch's commitment to its community guidelines, with many feeling that it sends a troubling message about safety and accountability.

item.title: Romania has declared a 30-day energy alert as Danube river levels fall too low to cool its nuclear reactors
item.description: In response to alarming low levels of the Danube river, Romania's energy sector is on high alert. Unit one of the Cernavoda nuclear power facility has ceased operations due to water scarcity. To maintain unit two's functionality, emergency measures including river dredging have been implemented. Authorities have also undertaken the blasting of rock formations to facilitate better water flow. Residents are urged to conserve electricity during high-demand evenings.

item.title: Rising temperatures are transforming Ireland into a rare wine country; the island now has 42 vineyards with upcoming bumper crops
item.description: As climate change enhances grape-growing conditions, Irish winemakers foresee a bountiful harvest. Expanding vineyards are drawing considerable attention from international investors. The unique interplay of soil and coastal weather is enabling the production of exquisite wines. To adapt to Ireland's cooler climate, new grape varieties are being introduced, with a focus on high-quality output to ensure competitiveness on the global stage.

item.title: Why did Lacy cancel his stream with Mark Wahlberg? Here’s what happened
item.description: Streamer Lacy opted out of a collaboration with actor Mark Wahlberg due to his desire for a more authentic interaction rather than a superficial promotional appearance. Upon discovering Wahlberg's previous engagements with other creators, Lacy felt disheartened. He reiterated the importance of genuine connections, ultimately deciding that the collaboration's scripted nature did not align with his vision for a natural experience.

item.title: Deepwater Horizon damaged deep-sea corals in 2010; NOAA is now restoring them 16 years later
item.description: In a groundbreaking initiative, scientists are working to revive deep-sea coral ecosystems that were harmed by an oil spill. Utilizing corals grown in laboratories along with advanced tools, they have successfully deployed these corals at great depths. This project focuses on rejuvenating delicate habitats in the Gulf of Mexico, with ongoing monitoring set to evaluate both the survival rates of the corals and the overall restoration of the ecosystem.

item.title: Harry Potter fans forced a power cable between UK and Ireland to be relocated as it would desecrate the 'grave' of Dobby
item.description: In a heartwarming victory for Harry Potter fans, a significant power cable, originally set to cross Dobby the elf's cherished fictional grave, was successfully rerouted. The Greenlink interconnector project, valued in the multimillions, was adjusted to preserve this beloved memorial. Developers resorted to horizontal drilling to lay the cable underground, safeguarding Dobby's resting place on Freshwater West beach from any desecration.

item.title: Michigan to remove the Sanback Dam in 2026, restoring 14 wetland acres and protecting more than 70 downstream miles
item.description: The historic removal of a dam in Michigan, over a century old, is set to rejuvenate the region's natural ecosystems. This collaborative project will facilitate the movement of aquatic life by clearing upstream habitats while addressing the environmental threats posed by polluted sediments. Restoration efforts will focus on enhancing wetlands and safeguarding vital cold water habitats downstream, fostering biodiversity and ecological balance.
